recipes.name: Isolde's German Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package non-instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9-inch springform pan.

Beat 1/2 cup white sugar and butter together in a medium bowl until smooth. Stir in 1 egg, then stir in flour and baking powder; knead into a dough. Press into the bottom and up sides of the prepared pan.

Combine quark, remaining 3/4 cup white sugar, pudding mix, oil, and 1 packet vanilla sugar in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in milk, remaining 1 egg, egg yolks, and lemon juice; pour into the crust.
Bake in preheated oven until filling no longer moves when you shake the pan, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Isolde's German Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: Isolde's German cheesecake recipe uses quark. Although you can substitute it, quark is the unique ingredient for this cheesecake, and it's worth it.

review.reviewBody: This was so much like my Oma's cheesecake I was floored! Luckily I found Quark, vanilla sugar, and non-instant vanilla pudding at a local German deli (Old Heidelberg, if you are in the Phoenix area). I followed the recipe to the T, except I added "drunk raisins" (raisins soaked in rum) to the batter, as my Oma does. It was fantastic. I am so glad that I can now make the cheesecake that I previously only had on trips to Germany. Thank you!

Lived in Germany for 13 years. This recipe nails it, hands down. Simple to make. Substitute farmers' cheese for the quark since that's impossible to find in the USA, except at Wegmans in Maryland. Note: I noticed in Florida, closer to sea level, the cake doesn't rise as much and needs to cook an additional 20 minutes in a 9-inch springform.

Made twice! Once with yogurt once with marscapone. Keep in mind if substituting other things for Quark- quark is zero to low fat! So if you are using marscapone or higher fat cheese like me the extra oil in the batter is not necessary! I used 16 oz. Marscapone and 2 ounces of sour cream to replace 18 oz. of quark. Instead of milk I used heavy cream whipped to soft peak - then folded in the cheese egg mixture. I used 1 tsp vanilla and 4 tbs of cornstarch in place of the pudding mix. Also you could add butter instead of the oil to the batter which would give a firmer end result if cheesecake ends up too soft. I baked until there was a slight jiggle in the center then covered and shut the oven off. Left in oven for 30 minutes before chilling. Wonderful! 2nd time - I used strained plain Greek yogurt - whipped cream just like I did with marscapone version, used butter in place of oil. I also used only half the amount of sugar called for. The greek yogurt version is my favorite!! Note! Both took a LONG time to firm up in the fridge 7+ hours but eventually they did! If top gets too dark while baking cover with foil.
We used Greek yogurt and baked for 2 hrs came out perfect. So others must have convection oven

I believe there are some directions missing from this recipe. When I made this cheesecake the bake time was significantly longer than shown and the finished cheesecake was too wet. Talking with Oma I discovered that she uses cream vs. milk listed here and whips it to peak, then folds it into the quark. She also uses 3 eggs in the cheesecake vs. one and two yolks shown here. I plan to redo this with the whipped cream and additional eggs. HTH!

Have not tried the recipe yet, but it reads about right. I am from Germany and bake a traditional german cheesecake almost three times a month. My husband just loves his cheesecake. You all know that it is very easy to make Quark at home, right? All you need is milk and some cultures an oven and a cheese cloth, if you want to make a big batch at once, or buttermilk and a yogurt maker for a small batch. I recommend the milk and the cultures, turns out just like store bought in Germany, if not better.

I just made it and couldn't hardly wait to cool it.
I didn't have any pudding powder so I used cornstarch, about 1 heaping tbl spoon. and did not use as much milk as directed, only about 1 cup milk and 1/2 cup French vanilla
coffee mate. I also used 1 container 32 oz. plain Greek Yoghurt, that I drained overnight over some cheesecloth, for the quark.
It tasted wonderful and will make again. Next time I will have the Pudding, but will use Yoghurt again. It turned out great

So amazing, completely authentic! Don't be concerned if it seems watery, it will thicken. Also, I didn't use a springform pan, and it turned out fine. However I would suggest a springform pan. Don't listen to reviews of those that used cream cheese, Unfair to rate something poorly because you used completely different ingredients! Lastly, if there is not a German deli near you, these ingredients can be purchased from Germandeli.com ; also if you are feeling adventurous - make your own quark cheese!

I use cottage cheese and 6 eggs no milk and a heaping tablespoon flour put all ingredients in a blander till smooth it works well
Nice tangy flavor. This did require 90 min to bake. I would suggest if you only like the crust on the bottom to cut those ingredients in half and do a 15 min pre-bake.
Totally authentic and tastes just like home 😊
Quark substitute: Combine 9 parts of Ricotta Cheese and 1 part of Sour Cream
I made this as directed and it turned out perfectly. It took longer to cook than the recipe estimated though.

I’ve made this twice now. Once using Clark, and once he is in mascarpone. They both turned out terrible! The cheesecake would not set up at all even though I left it in the oven for an hour longer than the recipe called for.

Am hesitant to say anything negative given all the praise - maybe it was the problem of my oven, but it turned rather brown, almost black on the surface... Tastes good otherwise, but will need to make it again with something like 160 degrees Celsius, as 175 turned out to be way too high, at least in my oven.
Excellent recipe, it turned out perfect. My German wife is very happy, you helped me earn some serious 'husband points' ??
Being German myself, this is authentic and delicious. I prefer cheesecake without the bottom.
